lesson.topicTitle: Structure and functions in living organisms

specAnchors.text: understand how the process of respiration produces ATP in living organisms
know that ATP provides energy for cells

primer.text: Respiration happens in every living cell, quietly and constantly. This note pins down what the process actually is — a chemical reaction, not the breathing that feeds it — and follows the energy it frees into ATP, the currency every cell spends on movement, growth and warmth.

modules.title: Respiration Is a Chemical Reaction
modules.opening: Respiration is the chemical reaction run by all living organisms that breaks down glucose — with oxygen when available, without it when not — releasing energy that is transferred into ATP.
keyPoints: Every living organism carries out respiration.
Glucose is the fuel broken down in the reaction.
Oxygen marks the aerobic version; its absence marks the anaerobic one.
Carbon dioxide and water are the usual waste products.
The released energy is transferred as ATP.

low.restatement: All cells break down glucose and bank the released energy as ATP.
low.analogy: A power plant burning fuel to send electricity down the line — the line here is ATP.
low.examPointer: Keep respiration and gas exchange separate: one moves gases, the other spends glucose.

medium.restatement: Whether oxygen joins or not decides the pathway, but both versions transfer energy, and the aerobic one also yields carbon dioxide and water.
medium.analogy: Two routes up the same mountain: one needs gear, one does not, and both get you higher.
medium.examPointer: If a question says energy is 'produced', correct it: energy is released or transferred, never made.

modules.title: ATP, the Spent Currency
modules.opening: ATP molecules forged during respiration are broken down again wherever work is needed, paying for reactions that build larger molecules, for every muscle contraction and for the warmth that keeps enzymes working well.
keyPoints: Cells produce several ATP molecules as glucose is broken down.
Breaking ATP down releases energy for living processes.
Building larger molecules from smaller ones consumes ATP.
Muscle contraction draws on ATP for movement.

low.restatement: Respiration fills ATP wallets; cell work empties them.
low.analogy: Rechargeable batteries: charged by respiration, drained by every job the cell does.
low.examPointer: List the three classic uses: building molecules, contracting muscle, keeping warm.

medium.restatement: The link runs both ways: respiration charges ATP, and splitting it powers the energy-demanding reactions that would otherwise stall.
medium.analogy: A household budget: income from work pays the rent, the food and the heating.
medium.examPointer: Match each ATP use to an example — protein building, a bicep contracting, shivering — for full marks.

glossary.definition: The chemical reaction in all living cells that breaks down glucose and transfers energy into ATP.
Adenosine triphosphate, the molecule cells break down to fund their work.
The movement of oxygen in and carbon dioxide out — distinct from respiration itself.
